approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from scored survivors and fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process to all real observations in the current session. It plans two batches together, comparing a Thompson batch with bounded alternatives and pricing an analytic conditional second-batch policy. Before observing the first batch it saves four mutation attempts per possible source. Saved offspring enter second-batch support only when one of their chosen first-batch sources survives the top-64 update. After real feedback it executes the saved conditional policy and records every purchase in the real archive.
approach.novelty: Remove the requirement that a saved offspring's first-batch source remain in the top-64 population. The offspring remains available because its graph was already saved and its source was really evaluated; its conditional value and mean eligibility still respond to feedback. Real survival and breeding stay intact. Earlier descendants introduced saved commitment, analytic tail integration and the bank as a whole; none isolated this extra availability gate, and the frozen request lists no same-Parent sibling.

observed_bottleneck: On the actual code Parent n-aedff97c8e9f, physically saved offspring become unavailable solely because their evaluated A source leaves top64. The complete Search provenance audit reconstructs all210 recourses:323 of2100 real A records are non-survivors, yet all retain exact trajectory-matched labels/serials in the next real fit. There are1240 already saved bank-only support occurrences excluded by this predicate over125 recourses;944 become final eligible under the same historical conditional means, with13 mean-mask displacements. Their unpurchased values are unknown. Parent has127/420 zero-progress windows,99/210 zero B batches and60 flat committed pairs, despite confirmed bank activation and full-window mean0.02430725541129775. Its endpoint0.5602580014730827 is +0.009650271640556984 over n-e68846780093, but this joint bank result does not price survival qualification separately. Preserve the bank confirmation and n-e68846780093 analytic-tail confirmation; n-59436e1eec8f's useful-progress refutation of alignment alone remains. Parent mean B valuation underpredicts by0.0028977212096408427; transporting its ancestor's mean-optimism diagnosis would be incorrect.

adoptions.applicability: The Parent already executes saved recourse correctly; its independently observed source-survival exclusions permit an isolated availability test without replacing that policy.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Condition the second decision on first-stage observations and value the rule that will actually execute.

deviations.adopted_setting: Existing bounded molecular support, noisy conditional model, batch recourse and16/16/32 panels; remove only the extra source-survival gate.
deviations.paper_setting: Continuous, noise-free GP minimization with a first-stage batch and one second-stage evaluation.
deviations.reason: Preserve the measured code Parent and isolate the ticket's support restriction; no paper performance guarantee transfers.

adoptions.implementation_change: Preserve external/observed_rollout.py conditional law and analytic policy; both allocate and execute_recourse use the same A-membership support, with real archive witnesses in optimize.py.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen review and its position1 adoption, checked against the primary paper. Keep observation-conditioned valuation/execution alignment. Internal Search evidence and archive provenance motivate testing the extra survivor cutoff; neither the paper nor a larger feasible set proves improved endpoint search. No assets, dependencies or new method are introduced.

sources.applicability: The existing saved recourse already conditions its second decision on first-batch observations. This node preserves that law and isolates a source-survival availability heuristic; the paper supplies no prediction that removal improves this graph search.
sources.finding: Two-step value accounts for a second decision after first observations; acquisition optimization accuracy and computational cost matter. A future action can remain physically available while its conditional value changes with observations.

hypothesis: Remove only the active top64 source-survival predicate from the Parent's fixed per-A saved-bank support. Availability is determined by a witnessed source's membership in the chosen first batch, independent of its observed or hypothetical survival; the identical real-data conditional law, mean mask and analytic policy still value and execute those options. Truthful accepted-A archive provenance makes non-survivor options physically executable without altering the live population. This can move pre-mask availability, final eligible identities and real paid exposure, which may improve full two-batch progress; it also identifies the signed conditional endpoint contribution of the removed gate.

finding_summary.headline: Removing source-survival qualification increased full-window progress and endpoint value
finding_summary.insights:
This exposed removal answers the registered contribution question: source survival had a negative conditional endpoint contribution on this bank and Search panel. It rules out the qualifier being necessary for the observed bank benefit under these conditions; it does not show that real top-64 retention, the saved bank or the analytic policy is harmful. The 22 newly enabled purchases yielded 6 source beaters, 6 losses and 10 ties, with 0 incumbent improvements and 1 identity later used for breeding. The total gain therefore cannot be described as immediate incumbent improvement from those newly available products. These paths do not isolate how much of the total score difference they caused: changed subsequent selections and descendants evolve together, and the passive alternatives have no purchased rewards.

The Parent's mean underprediction remains the relevant baseline: modeled-minus-real second-batch gain was -0.00289772 and is now -0.00105127. There are still 80 positive-model second batches with zero realized progress. Pooled modeled-versus-real rank correlation is -0.093, with 10 positive and 5 negative within-session correlations. These adaptive selected-stream diagnostics do not prove accurate ranking or a universal surrogate failure. A different conditional valuation or ranking model could address the residual mismatch; its advantage remains unmeasured.

The molecular evidence indicates continuing local exploration within familiar ring-rich aryl, amide and amine families: six whole paid trajectories and eight endpoint structures match the Parent. Murcko scaffold counts barely changed, from 1,762 to 1,770; unusual O-halogen attachments increased from 58 to 217 products, while small unsaturated-ring flags fell from 898 to 701. No configurations were specified despite 2,353 products with potentially unassigned tetrahedral centres. A proposal operator that preserves local functional-group environments and supports coherent ring/linker and configuration changes could address these measured coverage gaps; availability removal alone does not solve them. The borrowed observation-conditioned decision principle operated in both valuation and execution, but the noisy discrete molecular batch adaptation is distinct from the paper's continuous noise-free setting. This result settles the registered removal prediction, leaving wider bank development, mediated effects, chemical plausibility and independent reliability open.
finding_summary.results:
All 210 saved recourses and 110,880 planning scenarios reproduced the intended availability and conditional decision rules. On the Child's actual states, the old survival rule would exclude 1,258 saved product occurrences; 971 became final eligible after the unchanged mean mask, which also displaced 16 previously eligible occurrences. Total bank-only purchases fell from 784 to 777, while the optimizer actually bought 22 newly available products across 15 second batches. 6 of 15 sessions had no newly enabled purchase. Source labels, serials and nonlive ranks were truthful, and real population retention and breeding were preserved.

Mean realized best-progress over all 420 adjacent windows increased from 0.02430726 to 0.02463037, a gain of 0.00032312, passing the registered strict-increase test. There were 4 favorable, 3 adverse and 8 tied task/seed progress cells. First-batch gain averaged 0.01395065 versus 0.01248511; second-batch gain averaged 0.01106834 versus 0.01221134. Zero-progress windows were 121 versus 127, and flat second batches were 104 versus 99 of 210. Late incumbent gain was 1.747600 versus 1.777269.

Final mean Top-1 rose from 0.56025800 to 0.56478983, a paired gain of +0.00453183, exceeding the separate +0.002 target. Two seed means improved and one declined; endpoints comprised 4 gains, 3 losses and 8 ties. The code-Parent task-safety calculation passes. All 15 sessions completed; the formal Anchor comparison remains separate and its exact-code-Parent criterion is inapplicable.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aryl, amide and amine families retain unusual attachments, compressed ring topologies and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: This assessment reads all 15 Child and 15 published code-Parent Search trajectories, 4,500 accepted rows per side including 4,350 optimizer proposals. Both context.comparison.child_complete and paired_complete are true; no indexed trajectory is missing, and all paired initial molecule identities and scores agree. Six complete molecule/score trajectories and eight first-attained endpoint SMILES agree with the Parent; the other sessions change mainly within related structural families. The molecules are predominantly ring-rich and aromatic, not simple chains: 4,168 Child products contain a perceived ring and 4,051 an aromatic atom. Median size is 30 heavy atoms with four perceived rings; the range is 1-118 heavy atoms. The output covers indole aryl-amides, linked carbonyl/thiocarbonyl heteroaromatics, aryl/amine/ether/thioether rings, and N-rich cyclic carbonyl assemblies. Structural diversity is moderate: many graph variants exist, but favorable examples repeatedly concentrate around a few related families. Familiar medicinal fragments justify moderate rather than absent drug-like character, while unusual attachments and ring geometry make overall synthetic plausibility questionable. No synthesis, physicochemical assay, biological efficacy or toxicity result is inferred. Relative to the same Parent, N-halogen products are 778 versus 763, O-halogen 217 versus 58, O-O-bearing products 77 versus 59, and small-unsaturated-ring flags 701 versus 898. Thus one topology flag falls while several attachment flags rise; neither trend is a component-effect estimate or a universal quality metric. Explicit atom stereo, explicit bond stereo and assigned tetrahedral-centre counts are zero in both panels; 2,353 Child products versus 2,300 Parent products have at least one perceived unassigned potential tetrahedral centre. Only three Child products have formal charge in their graphs, so neutrality of the encoded set should not be confused with measured ionization. All numeric chemistry counts are derived from these trajectories using RDKit 2023.09.6, with definitions and full per-row records in policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-summary.json and its referenced per-seed audits. The original paths, byte-identical run-relative Child copies and SHA256 hashes are in policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/source-manifest.json. The full original trusted citation_trajectory_paths remain unchanged. Size, ring and motif flags are descriptive and do not certify stability or synthetic infeasibility; score gradients are associations among evaluated molecules only.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact indole-carboxanilide relatives: a fused aromatic five/six-membered core, a second phenyl group and an amide, with methoxy, methyl, methylamino, halomethyl and sulfur substitutions. Accepted optimizer products have median 25 heavy atoms, range 1-35, and median 3 perceived rings. The digest ring-closure/aromatic-text rates are 0.9483/0.9448. Each seed endpoint exemplar has 25 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. This is a recognizable medicinal scaffold, but much of its attachment chemistry is unusual: 420/870 products have an N-halogen bond versus 377/870 in the Parent. The Parent retains the same broad indole-amide family and size range; none of the three first-attained endpoint SMILES is unchanged. These are structural associations, not attribution to any algorithm component. Evidence files (Child copies are byte-identical to the frozen original Search paths): policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/search/child/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-aedff97c8e9f/seed-0/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/search/child/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-aedff97c8e9f/seed-1/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-zaleplon_mpo.json; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/search/child/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; nodes/n-aedff97c8e9f/seed-2/trajectories/zaleplon_mpo.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-zaleplon_mpo.json.
liabilities: Direct N-Br, N-Cl and N-F bonds occur on amide or aromatic-N environments; these require reaction and stability review and cannot be treated as interchangeable with aryl or alkyl halogen substitution.
N-amino amides, terminal N-S attachments and alpha-halo ethers complicate the otherwise familiar scaffold; graph validity alone gives no synthesis route.
There are 42 accepted products with at most five heavy atoms, including late elemental/interhalogen fragments with little of the favorable core.
missing_features: The favorable aryl-amide arrangement is not accompanied by systematic, chemically conservative attachment alternatives: repeated N-halogen, N-amino and N-sulfur variants dominate many favorable examples.

Coherent alternative cores that preserve the observed aromatic/polar arrangement are less developed than peripheral changes to the same indole-carboxanilide family; the low-scoring duplicated-core example shows that simply adding another core is not such an alternative.

The 61 products with a perceived unassigned tetrahedral centre have no explicit configuration, although the endpoint exemplars themselves have no detected tetrahedral stereocentre. The trajectory does not establish a stereochemical score preference.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxanilide at seed 0 evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145. The compact retained-core products at seed 0 evaluation 299, seed 1 evaluation 235 and seed 2 evaluation 297 each reach 0.44989726212142783. The first has an N-amino amide; the other two have N-bromo amides, with an additional N-bromoamino or ring-N-chloro attachment. Thus the observed favorable neighborhood preserves the aryl-amide core while changing its periphery, and does not distinguish ordinary attachments from N-halogen chemistry. Both a tiny ClCl proposal at seed 0 evaluation 282 (0.0) and the duplicated indole-carbonyl assembly at seed 2 evaluation 108 (7.489020749101934e-06) score poorly; more atoms or aromatic rings alone are not favored. The three corresponding Parent maxima are 0.4373696743346135, 0.46092619585962435 and 0.4478476056206344, still within the same scaffold family. No particular missing target pharmacophore is identifiable from these comparisons.

per_task.generated_character: The most extended aromatic series: median 38 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, range 1-118 heavy atoms; digest ring-closure/aromatic-text rates both 0.9713. Seed 1 enriches directly joined fused O/N heterocycles carrying carbonyl and thiocarbonyl groups, ethers, alkyl chains and carbon-bound fluorine. Its endpoint has 36 heavy atoms and four six-membered aromatic rings. Seed 0 ends with a 34-heavy-atom N-rich dione/aza-aromatic assembly carrying imine, thioether and oxime-ether connectivity. Seed 2 reaches a 52-heavy-atom azine-linked assembly with several aza-aromatics and a perceived nine-membered N-rich carbonyl ring. Ordinary heteroaryl/ether fragments coexist with difficult heteroatom linkages and repeated motif growth. O-halogen products are 184/870 versus 21/870 in the Parent, whereas small-unsaturated-ring flags fall from 242 to 25. Parent median size is 40 heavy atoms; the shared seed-1 endpoint is unchanged, while the other endpoint structures differ. Evidence files (Child copies are byte-identical to the frozen original Search paths): policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/search/child/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-aedff97c8e9f/seed-0/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/search/child/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-aedff97c8e9f/seed-1/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-deco_hop.json; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/search/child/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; nodes/n-aedff97c8e9f/seed-2/trajectories/deco_hop.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-deco_hop.json.
liabilities: Direct O-F and N(F)F environments occur near the high-score end and raise specific attachment-chemistry concerns; they are not ordinary carbon fluorination.
Large repetitive heteroaryl/ester/ketone assemblies and azine chains create substantial synthetic complexity, with no route or stability evidence supplied.
Some ring contractions produce small unsaturated fusions; the graph flag identifies review candidates, not a general ban on legitimate small rings.
missing_features: Compact, coherent replacements that retain the useful linked heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement without duplicating the whole assembly are underdeveloped: 195 products reach at least 50 heavy atoms, compared with 153 in the Parent.

Chemically conservative alternatives to O-halogen, N-halogen and extended imine/azine attachments are insufficiently separated within this favorable neighborhood; high scores do not establish those bonds as necessary.

Configuration is unspecified for 182 products with potential tetrahedral centres, and no alkene or imine bond stereo is explicitly encoded anywhere in this task. Whether any particular geometry improves the score is unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Tiny C=O at seed 0 evaluation 248 scores 0.5. A smaller peroxide-bearing quinoline at seed 0 evaluation 15 scores 0.5100965759438103. The linked fused heterocycles at seed 1 evaluation 284 score 0.6163726608089074, while the seed-0 imine/thioether example reaches 0.6056399007100387 and the seed-2 azine-linked structure reaches 0.6056676272814601. The 118-heavy-atom repeated heteroaryl assembly at seed 2 evaluation 228 scores only 0.5994161709627671: extension is associated with progress early in these series but unlimited repetition is not. Close high-scoring peripheral variants retain O-F (seed 1 evaluation 297, 0.6124567474048443), an N(F)F group (evaluation 300, 0.6121825779492125), or a compressed small-ring fusion (evaluation 275, 0.615221346270467). The visible objective therefore favors the extended heterocyclic arrangement without consistently excluding those attachments. Parent maxima by seed are 0.63430450550126, 0.6163726608089074 and 0.6057169855894164. These observations do not identify an unseen required fragment.

per_task.generated_character: Halogenated aryl systems joined to saturated or partly unsaturated amine-containing rings, with oxygen or sulfur bridges and alkyl/haloalkyl side chains. Median size is 32 heavy atoms, median four perceived rings and two aromatic rings; digest ring-closure/aromatic-text rates are 0.9609/0.9575. The endpoint examples have 30, 29 and 27 heavy atoms. Unacylated amines are clearly present: seed 2 carries aminomethyl and aminoethyl groups on an aryl-containing oxygen heterocycle, while seed 1 contains a cyclic tertiary amine and thioether. Seed 0 uses a chlorinated aminal connection between N-containing rings. These are not amine-deficient outputs. The chemically recognizable fragments are combined with less ordinary bridges, halomethyl attachments and stereogenic centres. Seed-1 and seed-2 trajectories are identical in molecule/score order to the Parent; seed 0 changes within the broad aryl/amine family. Evidence files (Child copies are byte-identical to the frozen original Search paths): policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/search/child/seed-0/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-aedff97c8e9f/seed-0/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-0-drd2_docking.json; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/search/child/seed-1/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-aedff97c8e9f/seed-1/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-1-drd2_docking.json; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/search/child/seed-2/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; nodes/n-aedff97c8e9f/seed-2/trajectories/drd2_docking.jsonl; policy/scratch/r0079-00-improve-L01/molecular/audit-seed-2-drd2_docking.json.
liabilities: The seed-1 endpoint contains two perceived four-membered rings with aromatic or multiple ring bonds in its compressed phenolic ring fragment. This needs geometrical and synthetic review rather than an impossibility claim from SMILES alone.
The seed-0 endpoint places chlorine on the carbon bonded to two nitrogen substituents; its local aminal chemistry is more unusual than the individual aryl and amine fragments.
Halomethyl groups and unspecified stereochemistry persist in favorable molecules. Formal-neutral graph encoding is not evidence of their experimental charge, reactivity or safety.
missing_features: Specified configurations are missing from the endpoint exemplars despite respectively 2, 4 and 2 detected potential tetrahedral centres; 834/870 accepted products contain at least one such unassigned centre.

The useful aryl/amine arrangements are not consistently explored through conservative ring, bridge and linker replacements. Some high-scoring examples instead add compressed ring fusions or chlorinated aminal connections.

All proposals are formally neutral as encoded. Relevant ionization-state coverage is absent from the supplied molecular representations, but the scores do not show which protonation state is favored or what the evaluator may infer internally.

per_task.generated_character: A relatively low-halogen family of alkyl/ethoxy-substituted fused aromatics connected to N-rich cyclic amide, imide and dione systems. liabilities: The seed-1 favorable structure contains adjacent [nH] atoms in a larger fused N-rich ring. Aromatic atom assignment is a graph-perception result, not evidence that this heteroatom pattern has a routine synthesis or preferred tautomer.
Medium-sized bridged N-rich rings and N-O/N-N links complicate synthesis and configuration control even when individual lactam/imide fragments are familiar.
There are 162 products with the small-unsaturated-ring review flag, versus 152 in the Parent; these require local structural inspection rather than a uniform penalty.

Topology changes that preserve the useful scaffold combination without duplicating large blocks remain incompletely represented. The visible gradient supports neither indiscriminate growth nor a missing specific target fragment.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
